standard.title: Statistical Investigations
standard.description: plan and conduct statistical investigations involving data for discrete and continuous numerical variables; analyse and interpret distributions of data and report findings in terms of shape and summary statistics
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have planned and conducted statistical investigations and communicated findings (from AC9M6ST03). Students can create displays and describe distributions (from AC9M7ST01, AC9M7ST02).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan and conduct statistical investigations with discrete and continuous numerical variables, and report findings in terms of distribution shape and summary statistics.

nodes.label: Planning a statistical investigation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students identify a statistical question, plan data collection (including variable type, measurement method and sample), and anticipate potential sources of bias.
nodes.minimum_width: Write a statistical question, identify the variable type and describe how data will be collected.
nodes.typical_width: Plan a full investigation including sample size, data collection method, and at least one potential source of variability or bias.
wider: Compare primary data collection (measurement, survey) with secondary data sources — identify advantages and limitations of each.
Investigate how sample size affects the reliability of conclusions.

response_modes.reason: Planning requires deliberate reasoning about the investigation process before data is collected. Students who skip planning rarely identify bias and produce poor data.

success_criteria: Writes a clear statistical question that can be answered with data.
Identifies the variable type (discrete or continuous) and appropriate measurement method.
Identifies at least one potential source of variability in their data collection.

nodes.label: Conducting, analysing and reporting
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students collect data, display it appropriately, analyse the distribution using summary statistics, and report findings in terms of the statistical question.
nodes.minimum_width: Collect data, create an appropriate display, calculate summary statistics, and write a brief report answering the statistical question.
nodes.typical_width: Conduct a full investigation cycle; choose appropriate displays and statistics for the variable type; report findings including shape, centre, spread and context.
wider: Use secondary data from a public source (e.g. Reconciliation Barometer, ABS) to conduct a statistical investigation on a social or cultural question.
Investigate: does the investigation support or refute a stated claim? Frame the report around evidence for and against.

response_modes.reason: Conducting and reporting a full investigation integrates all statistics strand skills. The integration and contextual communication are the learning at this node.

Statistical investigation only develops as a transferable skill through conducting multiple investigations in varied contexts. A single investigation produces performance on that topic, not transferable investigation skill.

success_criteria: Collects, displays and analyses data appropriate to the variable type.
Reports findings that address the original statistical question.
Uses distribution language (shape, centre, spread) in the report.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Secondary data investigations using real social or cultural data sets (Reconciliation Barometer, ABS) offer advancing students rich authentic statistical inquiry — the contextual meaning and ethical dimensions add genuine depth.
